An investigator would need to verify some points.","problems":["Headline says 99215 rate is well above expected 'in every complexity tier' and the rationale says 'two to three times' the all-provider share in every stratum; the card shows ratios of about 2.9x (0 conditions), 2.4x, 2.8x, 3.0x, 2.2x, 2.2x, so this is roughly OK, but the headline's 'every returned 99215 chart supported' overstates a 17-chart sample.","Rationale says 'the 24% problems-signal rate and the repeated-time flags (9%)' — the 9% repeated-time flag and the 24% problems figure do not appear on the evidence card, and the note-check line does not list repeated-time at all; these are ungrounded or inconsistent.","Rationale says 'The billing pattern points toward upcoding' and 'documentation points the other way' yet leans inconclusive; mixed messaging, and 'cloned data review looks unlikely' is an inference from only 2 of 32 notes.","Cited examples C0129314, C0129460, C0129499 are described as back pain, UTI and abdominal pain; this fits the dx codes (M54.50, N39.0, R10.9), but the summary cites only two claims in cited_claim_ids (C0128529, C0128559), which are hypothyroidism and hypertension cases that are weaker illustrations than the ones discussed.","'Against 0% for comparison providers' is correct to the card (all_provider_rate 0.0), but the comparison is trivial and the summary does not note that no below-billed examples exist to review.","Next step to request charts for C0128713, C0129182, C0129256 and C0129448 is concrete, but the structured next_steps list differs and names different claims, so the guidance is somewhat redundant and inconsistent."]}
